problem: Authorized chats/agents could leave routine protected promotion as follow-up instead of completing it themselves.
root_cause: Autonomous execution allowed release/deploy, but production promotion ownership was not an explicit universal obligation.
incident_findings: Parallel workers independently allocated the same Supabase migration timestamp, creating a global uniqueness failure despite locally valid changes.
Head-age based staleness can cancel healthy in-progress exact-head work and amplify queue thrash.
Concurrent terminal branch writers can race; non-force ref updates prevented lost updates during this incident.
PR metadata can lag the authoritative Git ref during rapid recovery; obligation plus exact branch/head identity is authoritative.
Duplicate active PRs for one obligation create redundant CI fan-out and must be consolidated.
prevention: Allocate final Supabase migration versions only at rolling-candidate integration and verify uniqueness before expensive CI.
Use per-run progress timestamps for stale detection; never cancel healthy current-head in-progress work solely because the PR head is old.
Enforce one obligation-scoped terminal writer lease; unexpected head mutation fails closed and rebinds to current exact head.
Treat PR number as transport identity; recovery follows obligation plus canonical branch/head and current main.
Parallelize independent specialist work but serialize overlapping paths, contracts and mutable resources only at the integration boundary.
Consolidate duplicate same-obligation PRs before terminal delivery.
